name: Anarcho-primitivism
scope: The anti-civilization current of anarchism as the defining sources present it: a movement that advocates hunting and gathering as the ideal subsistence and the band as the ideal social structure, rejecting civilization, agriculture and industrial technology (s1, s5). Its thinkers are chiefly John Zerzan, Derrick Jensen and Fredy Perlman, and its texts Zerzan's Future Primitive and Running on Emptiness and Perlman's Against His-Story, Against Leviathan. It excludes Rousseau and the earlier noble-savage tradition (an influence, not the ideology), the Unabomber manifesto (named as enunciating some tenets, but not an anarchist text), and green anarchisms such as social ecology that keep technology and agriculture.

summary: Anarcho-primitivism is an anarchist critique of civilization as a whole. It holds that the shift from foraging to agriculture and domestication brought hierarchy, coercion, alienation and ecological destruction, and that the state, work, the division of labor and industrial technology all grow from that turn. Adherents want civilization dismantled and people to live in small, egalitarian, face-to-face communities modelled loosely on hunter-gatherer bands, in close contact with nature.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: They would end central banks along with the state, but reject leaving money to the market, since money itself should go.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing specialization is a core primitivist demand, since it is seen as the root of hierarchy and alienation.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposition to all hierarchy and power relations includes rank by birth.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: They want governments and exchange abolished; Zerzan quotes with approval a way of life with no taxes or laws.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about abolishing wage labour, not money, and the statement now asks only about money; wage labour has its own statement.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Their common project is abolishing all power relations, structures of coercion and control, and they list governments among what could be dispensed with at once.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Zerzan calls for abolishing exchange in every form and the coercion of work, and counts wage laborers among civilization's enslaved.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Primitivists want technology abandoned beyond prehistoric tools, not accelerated.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Life-extension research is a prime example of the technological project they reject as part of domination of nature.

algorithmic-government.rationale: It would join technological systems with government, both of which primitivists want abolished.

alienated-labor.rationale: Zerzan's critique of work and the division of labor says civilisation alienates people from their own activity.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Zerzan approves a way of life where land is free and there are no governments, rather than state ownership.

allow-dual-citizenship.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Zerzan's Future Primitive criticizes domestication as a source of suffering for animals as well as people.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on research use of animals or on keeping animals rather than killing them for food, and the statement now asks only whether killing animals for food is morally acceptable under humane conditions.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Opposition to coercion, the state and organised religion rules out legal punishment for leaving a faith.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nulled: The saved primitivist sources say nothing on a state arming insurgents; the earlier answer rested on general anarchism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Moore's Primer rejects vanguard parties and Zerzan expects a mass break, not a small armed group acting for others.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Zerzan is hostile to modern medicine, but there is no stated view on assisted dying.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Zerzan treats industrial technology and the division of labor as sources of alienation, so building more machines to run society is the opposite of the primitivist aim; the goal is to abolish work, not automate it.

automation-leaves-most-without-work.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

ban-patents-on-life.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

ban-spanking.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

bound-labor.rationale: Zerzan treats domestication and agriculture as the origin of servitude and forced work, which primitivism seeks to end.

build-apartments-freely.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Primitivists reject all hierarchy and leaders, favouring direct, face-to-face community decision-making rather than any leader over the people.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Primitivists expect industrial civilization to collapse or be broken from its own ecological and social contradictions, and Zerzan treats its crises as terminal.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Primitivists hold that civilization, including capitalism and industry, is a regress that destroys autonomy and nature, not a foundation for a better society.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Anarchism opposes state censorship and coercive authority over culture, even though primitivists criticize art as symbolic culture.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning combines the state, mass society and industrial production, all of which primitivists want abolished.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Primitivists reject organized religion and all hierarchy as products of domestication and civilization.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its borders abolished, so citizenship of any kind has no place in their program.

civil-disobedience-accept-penalty.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

civil-marriage.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Zerzan and Moore reject progress and hierarchy, and see civilization as the source of domination rather than improvement, so rule in its name is illegitimate.

class-collaboration.rationale: They reject wage labour and employer-worker relations altogether and dismiss the left and reformism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Primitivists see domestication and civilization, not class conflict, as the driver, faulting Marxism for not questioning production.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and nationalism outright, so claiming land for a nationality has no place.

collective-defense.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its military alliances abolished.

collective-farming.rationale: Primitivists see agriculture itself as the original mistake, so they reject farming in any form.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Primitivists condemn civilization's expansion over foragers, but money transfers between states are irrelevant to their goals; the texts do not address it.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Primitivists want the state and civilisation ended, and colonial rule is the extreme form of domination they oppose.

communal-electorates.rationale: Primitivists reject the state, representation and electoral politics altogether, so any form of electorate is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Zerzan presents foraging bands as egalitarian and cooperative, and blames competition and domestication for hierarchy.

conscription.rationale: Primitivists want the military apparatus abolished and see organized war as a product of civilization.

constitution-recognises-indigenous-natio.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Their critique of civilisation holds that commodity culture and alienated work make life worse, and they urge abandoning it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: They want small egalitarian face-to-face communities modelled on foraging bands, but stress sharing and no property rather than formally holding it in common; many reject organised cooperatives as civilized.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies managing wages and prices expand both state power and the economy of work primitivists reject.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Primitivists side with peoples harmed by civilization's expansion, but state remedy programs are the reform they reject; the texts do not address it.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

criminalize-genocide-denial.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Primitivists want to end the state and its coercion, so a state criminal offence is rejected.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: They treat forager life as better than civilized life, so they would not say cultures are merely different.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: As anarchists who oppose all hierarchy and rulers, primitivists reject an official role for chiefs in national law.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its apparatus abolished but do not take up welfare's work incentives; the dependency framing is outside their critique, so they are indifferent.

decide-locally.rationale: Zerzan wants radically decentralized, face-to-face communities modelled on band society instead of mass society.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's claim to loyalty and oppose militarism, so ordinary people owe their rulers no support in wars.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and industrial production, so they would not defend a planned industrial state.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Zerzan opposes globalization and imperial domination but rejects religion and states; adherents have no stated position on religious duty.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Primitivists reject hierarchy and the state, so ritual submission and tribute between states is the opposite of their egalitarian, stateless ideal.

democracy-becomes-oligarchy.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

democracy-best.rationale: Moore rejects politics as government and Zerzan is anti-leftist; representative democracy is a form of state rule over mass society.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

dense-cities.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on preferring villages or the countryside, on land use, or on reasons other than the environment, and the statement now asks only whether dense cities produce lower greenhouse-gas emissions per resident than suburbs.

destroy-worshipped-objects.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Primitivists reject leftism, parties and any seizure of power, aiming to abolish power relations rather than capture them.

direct-action.rationale: Primitivists dismiss parties, elections and reformism as part of the system and call for a direct break with civilization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Zerzan treats gender division and patriarchy as products of civilization to be overcome, and Moore calls for ending power relations.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Zerzan holds up foragers' sharing as the model, though primitivists reject any system of distributing goods.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Zerzan rejects religion and all authority outside the community, so divine or popular sovereignty is refused.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Zerzan's Future Primitive treats the domination of nature and the subordination of women as arising together with agriculture and domestication, and Primer ties ending gender hierarchy to ending power relations.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Primitivists want an end to all power relations and hierarchy, so inherited political office is the opposite of what they seek.

elective-rulers.rationale: Moore's Primer calls for ending power relations and abolishing the state, so rulers of any sort are rejected.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Primitivists seek to abolish the state and all power relations, so state emergency powers are rejected.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Global governance extends the mass society and globalization that Zerzan wants abolished.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: They see civilization's domestication and social controls as stunting human freedom and favor spontaneous, unregimented life.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and written law as instruments of domination, so a constitutional document that empowers and limits a government has no place.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Egalitarianism is core: hunter-gatherer bands are held up as equal, non-hierarchical societies.

equal-outcomes.rationale: They hold up the sharing and egalitarianism of foraging bands as the ideal and see stratification as civilization's product.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Primitivists reject nations and mass society altogether, preferring small face-to-face communities.

ethnicity-statistics.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

exclude-trans-women-women-only-spaces.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Primitivists want industrial society dismantled and cities and industry abandoned, so expanding fossil extraction runs directly against their aim.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is a large-scale technological system of the kind Moore says demands obedience, and primitivists want such systems dismantled.

experts-over-public.rationale: Specialization and the division of labor are core targets of the primitivist critique, which ties them to the rise of hierarchy.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and its coercion, and condemn state violence as part of domination, so state killing of suspects is opposed.

farm-price-support.rationale: Primitivists treat agriculture itself as the origin of hierarchy and want it abandoned, and they reject the state, so farm supports are doubly opposed.

femininity-compatible-with-feminism.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Primitivists want states, taxation and money abolished.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and its military.

force-without-un.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its military apparatus abolished and see organized war as a product of civilization, so a country using force abroad on its own judgment is rejected, though UN approval is no part of their view.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Primitivists reject empire and state power altogether, so cultivating influence over former imperial territories is a project of domination they oppose.

four-day-week.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

free-trade.rationale: Zerzan calls for the abolition of globalization and sees industrial production as the engine of ecological destruction.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Ending hierarchy and power relations is the core primitivist aim, so unused arbitrary power over a person is itself unfreedom.

freedom-is-self-government-of-desire.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

future-generations.rationale: Ecological survival and ending the destruction wrought by civilization is central to the primitivist case, and it ties to deep ecology.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Primitivists reject state institutions and bureaucracy as instruments of hierarchy, so new government agencies are opposed even for egalitarian aims.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Primitivists critique gender and the family as products of civilisation and are divided on identity politics; no stated position.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Zerzan argues foragers had flexible roles and relative sexual equality, with gender hierarchy arising from domestication, and Moore speaks of gender constraints to be shed.

generational-constitutional-review.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering extends agriculture and domestication, which they hold to be the root of hierarchy and ecological damage.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

government-nudges.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

gradual-change.rationale: Zerzan calls for a sudden, uncompromising break, saying half a revolution would only preserve domination, and Moore rejects reformism.

harassment-claims-court-access.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Primitivists reject property and the state, so a stronger claim for a people over a land is at odds with them, though they do not discuss it directly.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Primitivists reject nation and state as products of civilization and treat written history as civilization's own story, so centring school history on a nation runs against them.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Primitivists reject nations and states as products of civilization, though they value deep attachment to place; the duty to protect an ancestral national land is rejected.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Primitivists reject property and domestication, which they see as the origin of hierarchy, so ownership by claiming land is rejected.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

human-enhancement.rationale: Technological enhancement deepens the alienation from direct, natural existence that primitivism opposes.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Primitivists reject property and work itself, so neither pay for work nor ownership returns is endorsed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Primitivists want the state and industrial technology abolished, so national nuclear arms are the opposite of their aims.

indigenous-internal-justice.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: They side with foragers pushed off their lands by agricultural societies, though critics say they romanticize indigenous peoples.

indirect-election.rationale: Primitivists reject all offices and want face-to-face decisions in small communities, not delegate chains.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Money, capital markets and private companies are all part of the civilization they want dismantled, and pensions presuppose them.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: This is the core claim: civilization, and industrial civilization above all, is the root of social and ecological harm.

industrial-unions.rationale: Unions are formal organisations tied to waged industrial work, which primitivists reject along with the left and reformism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Primitivists reject parties and reformist organisations and favour small affinity groups.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Zerzan and Moore trace hierarchy, gender domination and property to the same civilisational roots, so oppressions are treated together.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nulled: The saved primitivist sources say nothing on great-power intervention in allies; the earlier answer rested on general anarchism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Primitivists want every state abolished, so they deny any people's right to one.

job-guarantee.rationale: Primitivists want work itself abolished, so a state promise of jobs for all runs against that aim.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Primitivists reject industrial technology and the state altogether, so they want such weapons gone, not kept.

keep-public-institutions-small.rationale: Anarcho-primitivists want small-scale political structures: Zerzan calls for radically decentralized, face-to-face community on the lines of band society.

labour-priority-over-capital.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion and written law are both counted among the products of domestication and civilization.

leader-cult.rationale: Primitivists reject all hierarchy and rulers.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Zerzan and Moore reject the left as part of the system, treating the old divide as obsolete, though they do not seek a combination.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Zerzan wants the coercion of work abolished along with governments, so a legal duty to work is the opposite of his aim.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Anti-statism argues against criminal bans, but the critique of commodification and the objectification of women argues against the trade; the texts do not settle it.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

limit-growth.rationale: Primitivists treat civilization's expansion as leading toward an uninhabitable earth and want industrial production dismantled.

limit-population.rationale: Zerzan expects population to become quite low and Moore expects it to fall as women escape reproductive roles, but neither supports coercive limits.

local-production.rationale: They want small, face-to-face, decentralized communities living from their immediate surroundings.

local-veto-new-housing.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-steered settlement is a coercive tool of states and colonization, which they oppose; they back indigenous land and autonomy.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Primitivists reject the state's punishment and legal system as coercive civilization, so fixed state sentences are opposed.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: They would abolish exchange in every form and reject governments, and Moore says organizations are 'rackets' for putting an ideology in power; a party-led market economy keeps both.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Primitivists want production and the economy as categories to lose their meaning and call for abolishing globalization, so they reject markets as the allocator.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

means-match-ends.rationale: Moore rejects organizations and parties because they reproduce the power relations primitivists want to end, though insurrectionary currents accept sabotage.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Moore's Primer calls for abolishing the state, including its armed forces.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

military-superiority.rationale: They want military apparatus abolished and link organized war to civilization.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Primitivism rejects rule by any few or many state body.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Publicly funded systems presuppose the state, taxation and industrial services, all of which primitivists want abolished.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kings and priests are presented as the original agents of civilized exploitation and hierarchy.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Zerzan would abolish exchange in every form, which leaves no money to back.

more-religion-public.rationale: Zerzan lists religion among the products of domestication and sees ritual and shamans as early sources of domination.

municipal-businesses-mixed-economy.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

mutual-intelligibility-defines-language.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

national-church-status.rationale: Zerzan lists governments and borders among what could be dispensed with at once and treats religion as a product of domestication; a state-privileged church fits neither.

national-mission.rationale: They want the state abolished and reject nationalism, so no nation has a mission to export its government.

national-self-determination.rationale: Primitivists want every state abolished, so they deny that nationhood entitles any people to its own state; they prefer small face-to-face bands to nations.

natural-rulers.rationale: Zerzan stresses foragers' egalitarianism and aversion to rank, and the movement aims to end all power relations.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Jensen, cited as a key writer, calls the conversion of living beings to cash 'the central process of our economic system' and what must end.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Primitivists reject money, the state and its welfare machinery alike, so a state cash-transfer scheme runs against their program.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Primitivists reject capitalism and Marxist communism alike as forms of civilization and industrial society, and propose a post-civilized way of life.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They want the state abolished entirely, including the army, courts and police that this statement would keep.

no-central-bank.rationale: With exchange abolished in every form and governments dispensed with, no central bank would exist.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: With the aim of abolishing the state and all power relations, adherents deny that law as such creates an obligation.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Primitivists critique gender roles as products of civilization but do not discuss feminist politics.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Abolition of the state means no head of state, partisan or not.

office-by-exam.rationale: Primitivists reject hierarchy, specialisation and state institutions, so selecting officials by credentialed exam has no place.

one-party-rule.rationale: Moore dismisses parties and organizations as rackets for putting an ideology in power, and the movement aims to abolish power, not capture it.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

online-participation.rationale: Primitivists seek to dismantle industrial technology, and Zerzan rejects mediation through technology, so online politics is the opposite of face-to-face community.

open-borders.rationale: Borders presuppose the states primitivists want abolished, and band societies did not hold fixed territory against outsiders.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: The sources record no position on this, and no stated principle bears on it.

notes: Primitivists split on means: sabotage of industrial infrastructure is the 'more common' response (s1), while pacifist primitivists reject violence. Kaczynski is excluded from the scope. Themes searched in the saved sources: state, work, exchange and money, taxes, property, violence and sabotage, revolution, technology, science, religion, gender, nation and borders, decentralization. Answers resting on Wikipedia or on general anarchism (the Stanford entry) were repointed to primitivist sources or nulled.
